after:
Scrub the angle and watch the cursor on the s(θ) chart. During **dwell** the cam edge is a circular arc, so the follower stays still. The **cycloidal** and **3-4-5** laws begin and end each rise with zero velocity and zero acceleration. The **harmonic** law has an acceleration jump at the joins. A larger lift steepens the profile and raises the pressure angle. Lifts above the 30° limit, or that would compress the spring solid, are blocked.

*Idealized kinematics: rigid parts, no friction, clearance or follower jump. The spring force is only k·compression and is not a load rating.*
title: Cam and follower · programmed motion
before:
A **radial cam** turns uniform rotation into a *programmed* straight-line motion. The follower here is an in-line **roller follower**: its stem slides in a bushing on the upright, and a **return spring** presses the roller against the cam.

The cam profile is not drawn freehand. The model takes a displacement law s(θ), builds the roller-centre (pitch) curve, then offsets it inward by the roller radius. That is why the roller touches the cam at every angle.
caption: A radial disc cam on an overhung shaft drives a guided roller follower; a compression spring keeps the roller on the profile. The cam outline is generated from the chosen displacement law, so rise, dwell, return and dwell come from the shape itself.
